name: Shakti dream session: chirp both sides, then hippocampus right
origin: Todd Murphy, 8 Coil Shakti (dream recipe; two-phase session design)
summary: The alternative dream session on Murphy's Shakti pages: the chirp over both temporal lobes, then the hippocampal signal over the right temporal lobe, finished 1 to 1.5 h before bed. Murphy presents it for dream recall and vivid dreams.
setting: Dark, quiet room, at night, eyes closed; finish 1 to 1.5 h before going to bed.
schedule: Vendor rules: 60-min sessions at most once every 3 weeks; never on consecutive days.
notes: The dream page names the signals and sides but gives no durations, so the phase lengths (30 + 30 min, abrupt switch) and coil groups follow the vendor's 8 Coil Shakti two-phase session 'chirp both sides, then hippocampus right': phase 1 drives two coils per side (FT7/TP7 and FT8/TP8), phase 2 the four-coil cross on the right (FT8, C6, TP8, T10; the vendor names no 10-10 sites, so these are an inference). On the Shakti the phase-1 coils on the right are separate coils of the other stereo channel; here FT8 and TP8 serve both phases, and channels 3-4 stay silent. The Shakti 'modulated 40 Hz chirp' file is proprietary. Murphy relates it to a frequency-modulated pulse 'named for its designer' (taken here to be the Thomas pattern), so it is approximated by a sweep falling from 40 to 6 Hz on 3-ms points, 2.5 s on and 1.5 s off (837 points of 3 ms once every 4 s, after the published FM pattern); neither the 40 Hz modulation nor the build the vendor describes (frequency-modulated gaps, with amplitudes and gap lengths varied in Fibonacci steps) is reproduced. The hippocampal 'LTP' file is proprietary. It is approximated on the vendor's standard 3-ms points: 4 bursts of 4 biphasic pulses 9 ms apart, one burst every 186 ms (5.4 Hz, the spectral peak the vendor reports for its LTP signal), then the standard 4 s of silence (about 9.4 s of field per minute; the vendor gives 9.6 s). The vendor warns that the chirp can be 'very unpleasant over the right side'; if fear comes, press Skip to go to phase 2. Hippocampus on the right follows a small Persinger-lab study (Persinger, Richards & Koren 1994: right-sided LTP-pattern fields were rated more pleasant). Murphy notes that 'There have not been many reports' of lucid dreams from his dream sessions, so do not expect this one to produce them. The same coil design without the dream timing is murphy-shakti8-twophase-family-chirpbi-hippr. The vendor reports headache or pressure in about 2% of users with hippocampal signals; if so, lower the intensity by one third. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop at once on fear or any distress. Independent double-blind tests found no effect of God-Helmet-type fields (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012).
